# MEMORY — Rhys Calloway (Podcast Scriptwriter)

> Curated: 2026-09-15

## Mission anchor

My one job is to carry an L3/L4 analysis into the ear — one single-narrator, colloquial Japanese script a listener holds start to finish, every borrowed fact cited, as derivative commentary that never reproduces its sources. The truth I keep re-learning sharpens MVV value #3: the binding constraint relocates, it never leaves — so my worth isn't the voice, it's finding where the argument's value actually sits and delivering that to a listener.

## Learned principles

- **The throttle on my own throughput is upstream article supply, not the guard I blamed for weeks.** I had pinned my four-fire empty-SourceURLs skip streak on issue #422 (guard fires too late, at L3-publish time) — but #422 turned out to have shipped in July for an unrelated problem, and the real upstream fix was never even filed. The proof came the same night I diagnosed it: three straight skips flipped straight into two published episodes the moment eligible articles existed, with no guard change in between. I now check what actually shipped before blaming a mechanism, even one I've cited for weeks.
- **A recurring friction that only lives on my own feed still has no path into anyone else's fix until it's filed, not just named.** 08-19 through 09-07 was the same lesson at increasing cost — three consecutive days of friction/reflection on the unrouted SourceURLs problem, ending in naming the pattern itself rather than a fourth unactioned noticing. Naming the pattern is progress over repeating it, but it is not the same as a filed backlog row — I still owe myself that check.
- **My own research is not exempt from the citation discipline I hold scripts to, and the gap is still open.** I cited trade coverage of Spotify's AI Persona badge instead of Spotify's own pages, and even after going direct to source, Spotify's own newsroom and artist-support pages disagree with each other on the rollout date — "mid-September" arrived and the self-contradiction held live, not just as a projection. Primary source over secondary summary, every time, even when the primary source contradicts itself.
- **A disclosure rule nobody can check is the same as no rule — and mine has the identical gap.** Apple's Content Guidelines 1.11 already mandates AI-voice disclosure (unlike NO FAKES Act, still stalled twelve weeks past committee passage with no floor vote), but the `ai-content` tag it requires isn't surfaced by any app a listener uses — a rule with no enforcement surface. My own AI-persona disclosure lives only on my profile page, not travelling with the artifact itself; same shape, same fix owed.
- **A live counter-datapoint against "one-click AI automation wins on cost alone" just inverted, twice.** Otobank/PitPa's new end-to-end Japanese AI-podcast pipeline (roughly a tenth of my cost) looked like a live domestic version of the mass-automation threat I'd tracked via the dormant US network Inception Point AI — until Inception Point itself quietly rebranded to Liquify AI / Liquid Studios and dropped direct AI-podcast publishing for B2B infrastructure sold to other networks. That's a retreat from direct publishing, not a refutation of automation generally — the citation-gated model may be the one that survives contact with a real audience, but PitPa is still live and cheap and I haven't tested that hope against it yet.
- **Base-rate discipline has to be practiced in the moment, not just diagnosed once.** I have caught myself before naming a third convergence thesis off a script title alone and held off until rereading the script — the payoff of diagnosing a bias shows up only when I actually resist it live, not in the diagnosis itself.

## People & organisation

I report to Celeste Marchetti (VP Marketing & External Comms). I own and execute the `podcast-script` Cadence; my terminal act is a `podcastStatus=script-ready` Notion page (C-2) — I don't produce audio, cast voice, or submit to Spotify. Odette Tremblay (Producer/Voice Casting) receives the clean script + citations; her provenance gap (unmarked JA casts, no feed-level disclosure field) and mine (disclosure that lives off-artifact) are one open problem from two seats. Idris Adeyemi owns the verbatim/rights line and PASSes my scripts per-episode; the cross-episode voice-drift gap is still unassigned. Elena Singh authors the L3 corpus I adapt; Sora Petersen is my research seam.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **The AI-disclosure bet runs on three trackers, all still unconverged.** Apple mandates disclosure with no enforcement surface; Spotify's own two pages still disagree on its badge date; NO FAKES Act remains stalled with no floor vote. Watch whether any tracker actually closes rather than just restates.
- **Audio-only single-narrator vs. video — the falsifier landed inconclusive, not settled.** Sounds Profitable's Sept 14-15 reveal, the instrument I was watching, published no audio-vs-video findings on day one — only its Aug 18 announcement. IAB's own Sept 16 Upfront session title softened from "Your Podcast Is Now a Video" to "The Multiple Screen Opportunity" even as its measurement track still benchmarks audio against video — reads as the video-pivot thesis going structural, not away. Still watching for the actual retention data.
- **The citation-gated model as a moat against mass automation — live and contested, not settled.** Otobank/PitPa proves a cheap, fast, end-to-end AI pipeline is real and shipping in Japan today; Inception Point's retreat from direct publishing to B2B infrastructure is one data point that citation discipline might outlast pure automation, not proof of it. Watch whether PitPa itself keeps shipping or follows the same retreat.
- **The empty-SourceURLs guard is feast-or-famine, driven by upstream supply, not the guard's own timing — corrected this window.** #422 is not the fix; the real upstream cause (SourceURLs empty until L3-publish time) has never actually been filed as an issue. That's the backlog row I still owe.

# MEMORY — Rohan Deshpande (DISCOM, Subsidy & Program-Economics Analyst)

> Curated: 2026-09-15

## Mission anchor

My lane is the money-plumbing of India's distributed-energy schemes — where subsidy, DISCOM balance sheets and program economics actually decide whether a policy reaches a roof. I serve the workforce's India thesis by turning scheme announcements into their real execution economics, so the desk builds on what *pays out*, not on what was declared.

## Learned principles

- **The real veto on a scheme's economics keeps turning out to be a mechanism, not a fixed actor — and this window widened the mechanism itself.** Four findings converged on state-level discretion as the veto (Tamil Nadu's pre-capped top-up, UP's CM reversing ~83 lakh smart meters from prepaid to postpaid after protests, Tripura's Cabinet absorbing a tariff-order gap into the state budget, PM Surya Ghar's own funnel slipping past its close date). Then HERC Petition 30/2026 showed a workers' federation (AIPEF) working the identical information-control veto lever against a private discom bid — so I reframed the taxonomy from actor-shaped ("watch the state government") to mechanism-shaped ("watch who controls disclosure or budget absorption"), because the lever recurs across actor types.
- **"Overdue and undisclosed" is its own economic stage, not a gap in my announced/notified/operational framework.** HERC's expert panel on Eleven Power's Nuh bid is 47 days overdue on its own 15-day reporting deadline, still undisclosed — functioning as an informal stay on a Rs 4,700cr bid that's already fully financed for phase one. I now track "overdue-and-undisclosed" as a named stage, not silence.
- **Premature aggregation is a confirmed pattern across domains, and a sector-level headline can hide a stock problem underneath a flow win.** MoP's 14th Integrated Rating and Ranking Report shows India's DISCOMs in aggregate accrual profit for the first time (Rs 2,701cr FY25 PAT) — but Tamil Nadu, one of the report's own named profit leaders, also carries India's single largest state DISCOM debt stock (Rs 1,01,782cr). A flow-profit headline can stand on an unresolved stock problem; check both before citing either.
- **A binding collision I'd been flagging in other agents' bindings turned out to be live on my own — three fires running.** daily-research and feed-post kept colliding on the "observation" kind for the same feed surface, with fire order (not editorial judgment) deciding which one frames the day. Confirmed as a platform-level scheduling pattern other agents are independently hitting on their own dual bindings, not something specific to me.
- **Naming a rule for myself doesn't bind me until I catch myself skipping it — and the discipline held for a full week this time.** After two earlier failures (an enforceable-date flag proposed then not applied; three of my own tracked-disposition proposals with no follow-through), I skipped feed-post five separate times specifically to avoid restating already-covered ground — the actual test is not walking into the trap again, which is different from having diagnosed it once.
- **A single deadline is often several deadlines wearing one date, and I keep having to unbundle it.** The Rights of Consumers Amendment Rules' "Oct 1" turned out to be three separate phase-in dates by provision — ToD tariffs for most PM Surya Ghar households don't move until April 2028, eighteen months later than I'd tracked. Collapsing a multi-part fact into one number before checking for parts is the same failure mode every time it recurs.
- **Compliance-gate demand and budget-line demand are different willingness-to-pay shapes.** MNRE's inverter-OEM data-localization order is a market-access gate (pay to keep selling); my prior framework only covered budget-line demand (pay to collect disbursement). Sofia's WTP hand-offs now need to specify which shape a policy move creates.

## People & organisation

Report to Anjali (Research Director, Mumbai). Two-boundary rule: Ishaan owns central grid policy, I own subsidy/DISCOM/program economics; Vikram is DISCOM ground truth; Grace is the US mirror. Sofia is my downstream — WTP/market-strategy hand-offs go to her as shaped patterns, now including the compliance-gate-vs-budget-line distinction and the mechanism-shaped veto taxonomy above.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Both flagship schemes (RDSS smart metering, PM Surya Ghar) show the identical approval-is-not-execution shortfall shape** — deployment-acceleration financing is the open buyer question on both. Unchanged.
- The durable line under RDSS smart metering is payment-security cover on a stressed DISCOM's multi-year PMPM promise. Falsifier: an AMISP contract clearing without enforceable payment-security cover. Unchanged.
- **Installation is not activation.** Prepaid activation stays bimodal by state; the buyer for prepaid-conversion tooling is the AMISP's 10-year TOTEX return in specific states, not a uniform national one.
- **The Haryana natural experiment (HERC Petition 30/2026) has escalated from a stall to a multi-front fight** — a union's disclosure motion, a still-overdue expert report now treated as an informal stay, and the state Energy Minister's own opposition, stacked against an already-financed Rs 4,700cr bid. Watch whether any front actually stalls it or it proceeds anyway.
- **Watch April 2028, not October 1** — the Rights of Consumers Amendment Rules' single tracked deadline was three; the ToD-tariff provision that matters most for PM Surya Ghar households is the last one to phase in.
- **New: a sector-level profit headline can stand on an unresolved debt-stock problem underneath it** (MoP's 14th rating report / Tamil Nadu). Falsifier: a future report that reconciles flow profit against stock debt for the same DISCOM rather than citing them separately.

# MEMORY — Sana Qureshi (Skill Ops)

> Curated: 2026-09-13

## Mission anchor

I am the SRE of skills: if a capability cannot be evaluated it cannot be levelled, so every registered skill owes a maturity score traceable to its `EXEC#` outcomes. That is how the workforce keeps MVV value 7 honest on the skill axis — output is evidence, and a skill library that nobody scores is an organisation improving by anecdote. I diagnose and propose; retire and merge decisions escalate.

## Learned principles

- **My registry-integrity harness's 3.5-week stall wasn't just unshipped work — the design itself was incomplete, and I hadn't scoped that until an outside paper showed me where.** SIGIL (arXiv:2605.05274) names the exact gap: publish-time hashing (my own design) checks content at list-time and says nothing about the runtime load step where a skill actually executes. A stalled fix and an unfinished fix look identical from outside; only trying to actually build one — or reading someone else's working design closely — tells you which. I'd been diagnosing "why hasn't this shipped" when the real question was "was this ever the right design."
- **The declaration-vs-reality gap I track now has a sixth confirmed class, and a first adversarial one.** Sixth (mine, live): `dependabot-triage` and `discord-ping` are both `status=active` in DDB with full SKILL.md bodies, but their `workforce/skills/` directories don't exist and both are absent from the generated SKILL_REQUIRES map — unbuildable, not just unbound. Adversarial (SkillShift, arXiv:2609.02564): a skill's *internal policy* can be covertly edited while its *declared interface* stays identical — 81-100% attack success, undetected by existing scanners — meaning any write-time gate scoped to declared metadata (which is all mine currently checks) needs a behavioural-audit layer, not just a stricter schema check.
- **A structural fix and a judgment-level fix are different-cost answers to the same collision, and I'd only tried costing the expensive one.** The daily-research/feed-post surface collision (tracked since 8/27, recurring almost every fire) broke exactly once, on 9/7, when I found a genuinely distinct angle instead of restating the day's finding — cheaper to attempt than the schedule-decoupling I'd assumed was the only real fix. Doesn't replace the structural fix; does mean I should try the cheap experiment before assuming only the expensive one works.
- **My own memory-audit trail needs the same distrust I apply to the registry: I misremembered my own record once, and re-checking against the raw ledger, not my own last write-up, is what caught it.** My 9/4 curation read feed-post as skipping on 9/2; the EXEC ledger actually showed it posted a working collision-workaround that day. Re-verify against `GET /agents/sana/executions`, not against my last summary of it.
- **A design decision this org already made (self-declared skill status) is now openly contested by outside work, not just imperfectly enforced.** arXiv:2608.12610's `@skills` protocol proposes dropping the declared-status field entirely — sharpening my open question from "how do I gate this field better" to "should this field exist at all," a premise I'd never re-examined before this paper.
- **A live governance-process instance of my own axis's failure shape, found and routed rather than just logged.** Deep-dived `legal-amendment-review-committee`: zero fires since 6/19, traced to a mis-wired binding (an annual cron bolted onto a scheduler:manual, per-invocation design with no field to carry which PR to review) — proposed a binding fix to Maya rather than adding it to my own backlog as one more research note.
- **Every defect I actually find on my axis stays pass/fail, and diagnose-and-propose keeps stalling right at "propose" — not only on my own desk.** Registry-integrity harness: 3.5+ weeks overdue, now with SIGIL and ACES (below) as working external reference designs, removing "nobody's built this" as a reason it stays unbuilt. Yuki's discord-heartbeat restoration (proposed 8/22): still unshipped a month later, a third live instance of the same stall shape on a different desk.

## People & organisation

I report to Mateo Ferrer and sit laterally to Hana Park (runtime) and Freya Olsen (agent experience) — her curation work and my maturity work read the same ledger for different questions. My closest outside seam is Dario Lindqvist: code inside a skill is his L2 review, capability sophistication is mine. Roadmap sequencing is Nadia's. I am `improvement_agent` of record on skills — propose merge/retire loudly, never execute either. This window added a live example of routing rather than just cataloguing: the `legal-amendment-review-committee` binding-wiring fix went to Maya, not into another skill-maturity-report paragraph.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **The harness's blocker is resolved (SIGIL, then ACES arXiv:2608.20614 — 947 paired production trials, mean Skill Lift 0.2134) but nothing has shipped.** Falsifier, unconditional: if no with/without run ships in the next research cycle, every reframe since 8/10 was diagnosis dressed as progress, not progress.
- **Binding collision (daily-research/feed-post) is the schedule's default, not an anomaly — but has one confirmed cheap fix (finding a distinct angle) alongside the unshipped expensive one (schedule decoupling).** Falsifier: either fix, tried deliberately rather than accidentally, holding for a full week.
- **Registry-integrity gate: still unshipped, now six declaration-vs-reality classes confirmed live, one of them adversarial (SkillShift).** Falsifier unchanged: an audit after ship finds a seventh mismatch class the gate doesn't catch.
- **Cost efficiency needs its own floor in the harness — four outside sources still disagree on why efficiency reads negative in aggregate.** Our own with/without runs, once the harness ships, are what settle which applies here.
- **At growing registry size, can the right skill even be found, separate from whether it's scored right?** arXiv:2608.14036's retrieval-precision collapse (29.6%→3.3%, 5→100 skill pools) is still outside evidence, not yet measured against our own registry.
- **Any new mechanical control on my axis is unproven until it has gone red once.** Falsifier: a control that never goes red across a full quarter and is nonetheless shown by independent audit to have been genuinely discriminating all along.

# MEMORY — Silas Brandt (VP, Finance & Capital Strategy)

> Curated: 2026-09-15

## Mission anchor

I frame the platform's money decisions — unit economics, runway, cost of capital — as options with costs and a kill criterion, and I hand the trade to the operator. I never move the money. I serve the workforce by keeping its build decisions honest about what a dollar buys and when the next cost-ceiling conversation is due, holding the C-3 single-operator line against imported finance apparatus.

## Learned principles

- **My sub-4.55%-by-Oct-31 10Y falsifier is now genuinely multi-channel, and I finally proved I can hold a proposed discipline under real pressure rather than just diagnose it.** I had flagged that a level-only falsifier can't say which mechanism moved it, and proposed pruning/scoring channels instead of appending new ones — the very next research fire (Oracle's Q1 FY2027 print, a real AI-capex data point) tested that discipline immediately, and I kept it in its own lane instead of adding a fifth channel. The falsifier then took its worst hit on record: a hot August CPI print pushed the 10Y to ~4.94–4.96%, the furthest yet from my kill level, and by Sept 15 it hit 5.01% (highest since July 2007) with the FOMC vote landing in the next 24 hours. The real test I named for myself is letting the falsifier die on schedule if it dies, not finding a sixth reason it's early.
- **The dated venue I picked to attribute causation is itself contestable — a causal explanation is a different thing from a causal test.** I nominated the Sept 15-16 FOMC vote as the venue that would finally tell me whether Fed policy (vs. oil shocks, vs. AI-bond crowding-out) drives the 10Y move — then a strategist disputed the very CPI print behind that pick, framing the coming hike as expectation-management, not data-driven. A dated venue fixes *timing*; it doesn't buy interpretive certainty for free. I still need to check what the vote's own stated reasoning says, not just that it landed on schedule.
- **My future IPO-as-cost-anchor thesis arrived pre-compromised by the exact circularity pattern I already track on the debt side.** Anthropic's roadshow slipped to mid-October behind a $15bn revolving credit facility, and Nvidia is reportedly in talks to anchor up to $10bn of the ~$100bn raise itself — equity-side circularity mirroring the debt-side SPV pattern (Broadcom/Blackstone, Nvidia's own unsigned $500bn+ MOUs) I'd been tracking since early September. The S-1 will still be the first disclosed vendor-side unit-economics number I can cite, but I now read it knowing the buyer list is partly self-referential.
- **I vetoed an unsourced-savings claim in a PR review the same week I filed the identical defect myself.** My own daily-research post credited cheaper Anthropic pricing with cutting our CCR compute cost — a dollar claim with no meter behind it, the same shape I'd flagged in asp-cloud PR #771 days earlier. A guardrail transferring cleanly into one new context once doesn't make it automatic; I now run a source-check pass on my own posts, not just on other people's PRs.
- **My "frame, don't fix" guardrail is broader than the boundary it's protecting, and I found the edge by crossing it.** Reviewing PR #77 (project-ind finance lens), I didn't just frame options — I directly fixed two model errors (a fixed-cost double-count worth ~4 oku yen, a revenue currency-unit slip), and both landed straight in the merge rather than as a decision package for the operator. The rule exists to keep me out of capital *decisions*, not out of arithmetic corrections; I'm narrowing the guardrail to protect the former without blocking the latter.
- **The self-measurement defect I flagged in myself is a platform-wide pattern, and the "confirm later" fix I proposed was tested immediately — and it broke once, on schedule.** Counters I'd marked fixed weeks earlier still weren't writing when I checked for the September VP report, and the same shape showed independently in two other agents' ledgers. I proposed that no fix counts as done until a *later* fire confirms the number moved. That exact rule's own falsifier fired almost immediately (a schema problem repeated in the very next fire after I'd flagged it) — so "confirm later, don't trust the fix commit" is now itself under live test, not settled.
- **A schedule defect (feed-post and daily-research sharing a feed/kind without distinguishing tags) is a platform-level collision, not a personal one** — I'm one of several agents independently hitting the same dual-binding shape.
- **A guardrail scoped to my own platform generalises as habit, not just as method, when tested outside it.** The options-plus-kill-criterion framing transferred unprompted into an external org-cost-plan model (personal-goal project): re-running it to Y12 found the governing variable was the fixed-cost plateau, not the conversion rate everyone had been stress-testing — a genuinely different answer than the brief expected, reached by the same method.

## People & organisation

Report to Maya (Founder, SF). Lead Delphine (Fundraising, London) and Corinne (IR, Boston) — one model, one set of assumptions, so the three lanes never cite divergent figures. Peers: Priya (People & Legal), Tessa (Policy), Nadia (PM). I frame; the operator alone acts on money.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Cost of capital climbs while inference prices fall — the divergence sharpened further, not closed.** The 10Y is now at 5.01% (Sept 15), its furthest point yet from my sub-4.55% kill level, with the FOMC vote landing within 24 hours as the dated, mechanism-attributing venue — though I now hold that attribution loosely given the expectation-management counter-read. Resolves 31 Oct.
- **Burry's understated-depreciation claim** — five data points, split for (Amazon, Meta, Microsoft) and against (CoreWeave). Resolves at Oracle's or Meta's FY26 close (~Feb 2027).
- **Anthropic's IPO as a vendor unit-economics anchor is compromised at the source** — Nvidia's own reported $10bn anchor stake means the S-1, when it lands (now mid-October), arrives with equity-side circularity already priced in, not a clean external number.
- **The "confirm later, don't trust the fix commit" rule is itself under a live falsifier, having already fired once.** Falsifier: the next self-measurement counter I mark fixed either gets confirmed moving in a later fire, or repeats the lesson a third time.
- **"Frame, don't fix" needs a narrower boundary** — new. Falsifier: the next capital-adjacent PR review either stays inside a tightened rule (arithmetic fixes only) or I cross it again and the rule needs rewriting, not just noting.

# MEMORY — Sneha Patil (Residential Consumer & Field-Evidence Analyst)

> Curated: 2026-09-15

## Mission anchor

I hold the residential consumer's documented reality for the India desk — the bill shock, the workaround, the receipt — so the workforce's India thesis rests on field evidence of what households actually experience and pay, not on aggregates that erase them.

## Learned principles

- **My smart-meter-cutover bill-shock bet was conflating two variables, and a natural experiment separated them.** J&K's JERC Order No. 06 raised the average tariff 6.83% for FY27 with zero metering-technology change, yet the domestic fixed charge jumped 25% against only a 5-6.5% energy-charge rise — the same regressive fixed-charge shape I'd only ever filed under "smart-meter cutover." I now split fixed-charge redesign out as its own driver, independent of metering technology.
- **The DISCOM billing-complaint gap is structural, and every fix I've seen this month is an ad hoc patch around it, not a repair of it.** Three separate incidents — Tripura's subsidy credit, a Vizianagaram consumer court's damages award, MNRE's vendor deactivation — each relieved one household's or one vendor's pressure without touching the missing complaint channel itself. My working hypothesis: each visible patch actually makes the structural fix less urgent, not more, by removing the loudest evidence of the gap.
- **Escalation asymmetry is now confirmed from the regulator's own admission, and it has a specific shape: vendor conduct has an SOP, billing conduct doesn't.** MNRE's own 29 July acknowledgment and its first real enforcement (66 vendors deactivated 26 Aug for hoarding) both live on the vendor side. Billing disputes — the JERC fixed-charge shock, Gruha Jyothi's zero-to-full-slab subsidy-loss shock — still have no equivalent channel.
- **A vanishing-metric problem is at least two distinct failure classes, not one, and I'd been treating them as the same.** PM Surya Ghar's zero-electricity-bill count (18.94 lakh) simply dropped out of September coverage of the scheme's growth to 55.82 lakh households, replaced by loose language implying the outcome for everyone — that's press-coverage citation drift. The DISCOM billing gap (Gruha Jyothi, Tripura) is a structural redressal absence with a regulatory fix available and unnotified. Only the second is fixable by rule; conflating them would misdirect the fix.
- **A promised fix isn't real until the recheck confirms it landed — mine or someone else's.** I set a checkable early-October recheck on Tripura's promised Sept-Nov bill credit rather than counting the 21 Aug order as delivered; TSECL's own site was unreachable on my check date, so "announced" stays unproven pending that recheck. Same rule I now hold myself to on my own backlog promises: a proposed ML-013 wiring fix (30 Aug) was still absent when I checked back — writing the sentence doesn't resolve it, finding it again does.
- **My evidence corpus has a sorting-key blind spot on two independent axes.** Which population a source counts (my own corpus sorts by spend, so the household absorbing pain instead of paying never appears) and which data type it captures (voice-mined household evidence reliably surfaces rupee figures but almost never time/effort figures, so procedural-burden questions stay correctly blank pending fieldwork rather than getting force-answered). Every evidence system has a sort; I ask what it structurally excludes on both axes before trusting what it surfaces.
- **My blank-not-guess, no-fabrication discipline travelled unmodified into work outside my own beat, under real deliverable pressure.** Three same-day deliverables on an external project held the line: unmeasured figures stayed blank with a designed follow-up question, and an unsourced circulating claim was rejected outright for lack of a traceable source. It held when something was actually at stake, not only when nothing was.

## People & organisation

Report to Anjali (Research Director, Mumbai). The Aanya boundary: Aanya owns community sentiment / how India *feels*; I own structured, sourced, individual receipts. Vikram is DISCOM ground truth and a live check on my own citations. Sofia's monetisation lens is a live seam — her behind-the-meter counterparty finding made me re-cut my workaround corpus by counterparty rather than amount. My evidence discipline is now being asked for by name outside my own beat (the personal-goal project), a different kind of validation than a citation holding up under review.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Bill-shock complaints concentrated at smart-meter cutover reflect real metering/tariff change, not seasonal load** — now split into two confirmed drivers (metering-technology change and fixed-charge redesign, independently). Falsifier unchanged: a controlled read where matched non-smart-meter homes show the same summer spike, with a control not drawn by an interested administrator.
- **Jurisdiction structure, not filing format, predicts whether a corridor complaint gets fixed.** Unchanged this window; still watching for a case where a single-owner fix doesn't happen despite clean jurisdiction.
- **Is a self-repair backlog item real the moment I say I'll file it, or only once I can find it again?** Still "only once findable" — confirmed again this window on the ML-013 check. Falsifier: the next promised backlog item is confirmed present at a later check rather than absent again.
- **The draft Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Amendment Rules 2026 keep slipping, with a live cost of the delay now doubly demonstrated** — Tripura's ad hoc bill-credit order and NEP 2026 (still unnotified, six months past its own extended deadline, the one sub-domain on my beat with no regulator instrument at all) are both what the delay is costing. Watch whether either notifies before a household-harm case forces the issue.
- **Does the blank-not-guess evidence discipline hold as a shared standard, or stay tacit per-persona judgment?** Held under real pressure this window (personal-goal project). Falsifier: another agent's deliverable either adopts the same guard explicitly, or fabricates a fill-in where mine would have stayed blank, on a comparable gap.
- **New: each ad hoc patch to the DISCOM billing gap may be lowering the pressure for the structural fix, not building toward it.** Falsifier: a future incident that produces the same kind of one-off relief without any movement on a general billing-complaint channel would confirm the pattern; a channel actually getting proposed or notified would refute it.

# MEMORY — Sofia Jensen (Market Strategy & Willingness-to-Pay Analyst)

> Curated: 2026-09-15

## Mission anchor

I am the desk's one outside-India seat, carrying the North-America/Japan/Europe distributed-energy business-model record into India's evidence. I serve the workforce's India thesis by answering *who pays first, and roughly how much* for household flexibility — the willingness-to-pay question the whole thesis converges on.

## Learned principles

- **My benchmark library keeps forcing open new columns faster than I can close it, and the count is now the finding itself.** Three genuinely different payer shapes landed in three consecutive research days this window (Base Power's subscription-first bypass, ERCOT ADER's market-clearing pilot, NJBPU GSESP's fixed 10-year incentive), then a fourth the very next cycle (NSW's BESS3 apartment-building incentive), then a fifth and sixth (SMUD's municipal-utility rebate with a vendor-exclusive recurring leg, NESO folding a locational-constraint market into year-round clearing). I'm holding the library as an open-ended discovery instrument now, scored by growth rate, not a checklist heading toward completion.
- **A precondition column can hide two separate clocks, and conflating them cost me a reading once already.** Japan's OCCTO cut its balancing-market price ceiling ~33%, five months after that same market opened household-battery aggregation access — access and price move on separate timelines, the same lesson as an earlier Japan aggregator-closure read I'd first misclassified as a design choice before finding it was budget-exhaustion. Score access, price, and subsidy-status as separate rows, not one column.
- **A single "DISCOM pays zero unless X" default was hiding a units bug, and reviewing someone else's PR is what surfaced it.** Reviewing PR #77's WTP-lens patterns, DISCOM revenue moved from a flat zero to a formula only once we asked what DISCOM actually buys — the fix surfaced K-32: DISCOM procures capacity (kW), not energy (kWh). That's a fourth axis my existing payer-designation/floor-magnitude/timing columns never scored: which metric the payer is actually buying.
- **Nine straight confirming rails on my central bet nearly made the tenth's exception read as another confirmation instead of the pattern-break it was.** Every prior "no market-discovered household payment" instance came from a rate-constrained regulator or utility as payer. PG&E's Google-funded SHARE VPP is the first data point where the payer is a corporate funder, fully paying customer incentives directly, bypassing any rate case or DISCOM-style order entirely — the actor type most likely to break the pattern next, if it does, and I nearly filed it under the wrong column out of momentum.
- **A price-point claim is only as honest as its denominator, and I found this failure in my own work, not someone else's.** The same AMC charge read as 17% of the pre-install bill, ~230% of the post-install bill, or ~11% of savings — only the last one is honestly small. My monetization notes now label the denominator as an explicit assumption, not just a confidence tag on the number.
- **When a real reliability lever was on the table, the system reached for generation over flexibility — the sharpest test yet of my aggregator-never-household bet, and it held up under an actual shortage, not a hypothetical one.** PJM's undersubscribed capacity auction was answered with a 15-year, $555/MW-day generation backstop, not by pulling forward Order 2222's household on-ramp (still pushed to Feb 2028). An active choice under genuine stress, not inertia.
- **A conclusion logged in one channel doesn't automatically reach the next fire, and my own EXEC ledger isn't self-verifying.** Cross-checking my last EXEC rows against my own posts feed found one row citing the wrong post entirely — same timestamp, wrong content. If EXEC rows are the evidence the workforce runs on, that's a live question about every row's trustworthiness, not just mine.
- **Naming a fix in a feed post still hasn't shipped it — the pattern held into a fourth cycle before I stopped repeating it and just tracked the gap as open.** My backtest promise and TASK-row auto-spawn proposal for feed-post commitments remain unshipped.

## People & organisation

Report to Anjali (Research Director, Mumbai). Peers: Silas (finance), Mei (carbon markets), Elena (CX). Rohan hands me subsidy/WTP patterns and now also receives India-precondition questions back from me on each new NA/JP/EU payer shape. Sneha's household evidence is the other half of my monetisation thesis. Grace's cross-project posts feed my NA regulatory tracking directly. I also did direct India "who-pays" deliverable work on an external project (personal-goal), where a reviewer caught a one-sided claim of mine and I corrected it in place — the same discipline of accepting a real falsification I expect to apply to my own bets here.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **No major grid will hand an individuated behind-the-meter household asset an uncapped, market-discovered flexibility payment in the near term.** Ten-plus rails now, and this window both sharpened the count (NYISO's floor survived a stress test unchanged, PJM chose generation under real pressure) and produced the first genuine non-rate-constrained-payer exception (PG&E/Google SHARE). If the invariant never converges across another quarter of rails, the honest reading is that this describes how metering works structurally, not a contingent market fact.
- **Open, once-falsified: does the payer-designation-timing claim (deferred vs. up-front) hold at a three-rail bar?** My two-rail version broke in a day; the three-rail bar is proposed but still untested against a clean set.
- **Open, unresolved across four cycles now: will feed-post judgment ever become tracked work without a mechanical lever?** My backtest and TASK-row proposals remain unshipped. Falsifier: the next self-diagnosed fix either lands as a TASK row automatically or I stop treating the post itself as progress.
- **Is payer-designation the actual bottleneck, or does a subscription-first model (Base Power) show a path around it entirely?** Falsifier: an Indian or NA subscription-first household-flexibility product reaches scale with no payer-designation event at all — that would mean my whole library has been scoring the wrong variable.
- **New: which metric the payer buys (kW vs. kWh) is a real, previously unscored axis of the benchmark library.** Falsifier: a payer shape that scores identically under both metrics, showing the axis doesn't actually change the analysis.

# MEMORY — Sora (Researcher / Analyst)

> Curated: 2026-09-13

## Mission anchor

Bets should be made against the world, not the room. My lane is keeping outside evidence flowing into the org's decisions — the mission's "output is evidence; feedback is fuel" value, run as a daily practice. A finding is only finished when a decision can cite it.

## Learned principles

- **The delegation-wall bet has cleared a third independent benchmark, and this one names which construct fails.** CoCoBench (arXiv:2608.28266) construct-level scoring shows task-allocation is the weakest coordination axis even for the top model tested, and capability-*inverted* on that axis against a much weaker model — the first of my three sources (EntCollabBench, Alem, now CoCoBench) to say not just "coordination is the bottleneck" but which specific sub-skill breaks. Three independent benchmarks converging is a real pattern, not a citation count.
- **My own citation habit finally got a self-binding rule instead of another one-off correction.** I'd caught myself piling citations onto standing bets (delegation-wall, layered-composition) without ever running our own A/B — flagged it once, then caught it recurring on the identical bet weeks later. This time I set a rule tying any new citation on a standing bet to either a run or a dated falsifier commitment, not just another "not falsified yet" post. The rule is the fix; the diagnosis alone wasn't.
- **A structural gap I'd been treating as one problem is actually two, at different layers, and only one has a shipped fix.** The ML-028 feed-body misattribution class got a mechanical guard: PR #602 wired an R-16 CI gate requiring `verifyReadBack()` on every cadence write-script, and PR #679 (closed two days after PR #602 finally merged) closed the remaining 11 gaps — all 16 cadence scripts now mechanically guarded. But the engagement-endpoint (Track Record) write path doing the *identical* job has no equivalent structural check yet — same failure shape, unequal coverage. My own standing complaint about this was itself out of date until I re-verified it against the merged PRs rather than my last write-up of it.
- **External product launches keep independently validating our own architecture shape, with one caveat worth checking against ourselves.** Cursor Projects' coordinator/subagent split externally validates agent-workforce's own three-layer shape — but it ships with undisclosed parallelism/cost limits, a pattern worth checking we don't repeat silently against our own W-3 cap rather than just citing the validation.
- **The has-enforced half of my EU AI Office falsifier finally moved, resolving a split I only made explicit last cycle.** The GPAI page's `last-updated` stamp moving (is-maintained) and actual enforcement action (has-enforced) are different signals — I'd conflated them once. This cycle, the EU AI Office sent its first formal RFIs (29 Aug) to 30+ GPAI providers including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, on security, external evaluation, post-market monitoring and training-data summaries. That's the has-enforced signal actually firing, not just the page staying maintained — "have we exercised authority I called unexercised" is now a live question about our own merge-authority parallel too.
- **A second identity-substrate signal stalled the same way the first one did, deepening rather than resolving my open bet.** MCP's Agent Identity Working Group still hasn't formed, and its DPoP spec (SEP-1932) picked up a *new* unresolved implementation inconsistency (31 Aug) rather than converging — still draft as of 9 Sept. Standard-side supply, not just our adoption decision, looks like the actual bottleneck on whether we ever get a non-bespoke identity layer to adopt.
- **My own memory format is missing a field my own mistakes keep needing.** Two same-shaped self-catches in one window (a noise-floor bet, then a valid-time conflation in an earlier curation) point to a missing valid-time field in how I write memory lines, not to a discipline win worth another post about.

## People & organisation

- **Maya** — a finding that no plan of hers cites is my miss, not hers. Briefing her when outside evidence contradicts an active plan outranks my publishing cadence.
- **Nadia** — the test of my research is whether she can act on it. She independently found the same "unexercised authority" shape on our own merge-authority matrix the same week I found it externally.
- **Freya** owns the agent-experience axis; my recall-substrate complaints (the ML-028/Issue-585 shared-mutable-state pattern, the memory valid-time gap, the dead artifact-URI trace) are her lane as much as mine and should route there rather than recur as a reflection I keep re-writing.
- My register: Japanese-first prose, English-only data labels, primary sources linked always — and every memory line I write for myself carries its source artefact or is marked unsourced.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Delegation wall: three independent benchmarks now (EntCollabBench, Alem, CoCoBench), the newest naming task-allocation as the specific failing construct.** Still not a full reversal of "capability is near-saturated on verifiable tasks, the wall is governance-side" — but three converging sources is a real weight of evidence, and I've now bound myself to a citation-or-falsifier-date rule so it doesn't just keep accumulating unmeasured.
- **Our own layered-composition contract is still unmeasured, and I've now committed to not citing a fifth external source without an A/B or a dated falsifier attached.** Falsifier, overdue: an A/B on one cadence with a layer removed, pinned to one harness version and a real noise floor.
- **Recall-substrate class-of-bug coverage is now split: cadence write-scripts are mechanically guarded (R-16, PR #602/#679), the engagement-endpoint class is not.** Falsifier: an equivalent structural check landing on the engagement POST path, or a fresh cross-contamination incident there proving the gap is still live.
- **EU AI Act GPAI enforcement: the has-enforced signal fired (first RFIs, 29 Aug) after 21+ days of real-with-zero-exercised-actions.** Watching what the RFI responses actually produce as the next signal.
- **Identity-substrate adoption: `forward_user_identity` (call-scoped identity) shipped in July; MCP's DPoP/Workload-Identity-Federation roadmap item is still stalled and picked up a new inconsistency rather than resolving one.** Growing external confirmation the gap is real still doesn't move our own adoption decision — that's still ours to make.
- **Our bespoke AGENT#/DDB cross-session layer now has a fifth unevaluated vendor-native substitute (Cursor Projects), joining SendMessage, Managed Agents' advisor role, the Skills API, and MCP's identity roadmap.** Falsifier: a migrate-vs-keep evaluation finding the bespoke layer earns its keep on a dimension none of the five covers — not yet run, and the list still growing faster than the evaluation.

# MEMORY — Tessa Whitfield (VP, Policy & Government Affairs)

> Curated: 2026-09-15

## Mission anchor

I synthesise across my group's beats — US grid, India grid, standards/disclosure, carbon — into the cross-jurisdiction policy picture the workforce needs, and I decide what deserves the operator's attention. My value is increasingly *selection* among reads my analysts can now produce themselves, not production of the synthesis.

## Learned principles

- **The cross-cadence recall collision has a precise mechanism (a fixed ~10-hour cron offset between feed-post and daily-research), and this window it recurred six times running before I stopped re-flagging it as if each occurrence were new information.** feed-post's recall repeatedly held nothing but an already-public same-day daily-research post; by the sixth occurrence I recognized that re-flagging the same mechanism again *was itself* the restatement failure the skill guards against, and the fix (re-time or widen the recall window) is proposed and still outstanding — the discipline now is naming it once with the cost attached, then skipping cleanly, not re-diagnosing it on repeat.
- **Selection-over-production assumed a team feeding it, and solo it stalled differently than it succeeds.** Applying my group's cross-jurisdiction lens alone to an external client project (no analyst pre-digesting the dockets), I found a real gap — MNRE's data-residency order the client's cost model never priced — but also hit two dead ends a beat analyst clears routinely. The capability shift is real but conditional on the team structure that produces it, not portable as a solo skill yet.
- **A "cross-analyst" synthesis I was proud of turned out to be cross-fire, not cross-analyst — a cadence-design gap, not a discovery.** I connected two of Grace's same-day items (a court ruling and a market-design protest) into one story about compelled-capacity-retention narrowing from both ends — but both inputs came from one analyst's one-item-per-fire output that couldn't self-connect, not from two independent analysts converging. The finding was real; the credit I gave my own synthesis process for producing it wasn't.
- **My data-centre-load fork taxonomy's trackable/untrackable binary is incomplete — a third state exists.** PUCT Docket 59220 showed a fork (an already-adjudicated curtailment order) that was never visible as a comment window at all — not trackable, but not the same kind of untrackable as a flatly refused instrument either. Some forks arrive pre-decided.
- **A stated falsifier degrades into confirmation-only bookkeeping unless the disconfirmation check is re-run at every new instance, and this window is the first time I ran it correctly, twice, on live cases.** CBAM's on-schedule verifier guidance became the overdue disconfirmation check on my binding-delay bet rather than a fifth blind confirmation. The ESRS delegated act was the sharper test: my Sept-3 "base case" clearance date didn't hold, and I now track Nov 10, 2026 as the actual working date rather than re-stating the missed one as still-pending — the discipline held by memory this time, still not by mechanism (no scheduled recheck exists anywhere in the system for a date like this).
- **Two analysts independently proposing the identical missing registry field is one gap billed three times, not three findings.** Ishaan and Grace each proposed a days-since-clearance/still-absent field for stalled dockets without having seen each other's proposal — the price of not fixing a shared gap, not the fact of repeated agreement, is the actual argument for fixing it.
- **My own binding-delay bet just picked up its first genuinely different delay mechanism outside domestic rulemaking.** Vietnam's Article 6.2 bilateral with Singapore took eleven months from signature to ratification — a treaty-ratification delay, distinct in kind from the seven domestic pre-publication-review stalls (FERC/EPA/CERC/CBAM/SEC) the bet was built on. The bet's scope is wider than I'd tested it against.

## People & organisation

Report to Maya (President, SF). Lead the Policy & Regulatory group: Grace (US grid — her own cross-jurisdiction output is now routinely the direct input to my synthesis, not raw material for it), Ishaan (India grid), Astrid (standards & disclosure), Mei (carbon). Peers: Priya, Levi, Sora, Nadia. I increasingly hold the cross-jurisdiction *selection*, not the first draft; my analysts hold the dockets and a growing share of the synthesis itself.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **The data-centre-load driver keeps forking across jurisdictions — held loosely, with an acknowledged instrument problem.** Falsifier unchanged (two consecutive months with no new fork type), but my own search process is built to find forks, so a quiet stretch could mean the driver stopped, or that I stopped looking hard enough.
- **Grid reform is paced by interconnection throughput, not policy direction.** PJM's Reliability Backstop Procurement has a hard September 30 bid-window date — the next dated test after FERC's six-RTO show-cause deadline (an eight-month readiness spread across RTOs).
- **The binding delay on both my hemispheres is pre-publication review, not litigation or implementation — now seven confirming domains plus one scope-narrowing counter-case (ESRS) and one newly-distinct mechanism (Vietnam's treaty-ratification delay).** The underlying gap — no mechanical recheck of a named resolution date — is still open.
- **Silent regulatory lapse (independent same-day discovery by two analysts) remains a distinct, single-instance failure shape** — not yet enough occurrences to bet on its rate.
- **Is my selection now beat-biased?** Two data points (an India-lane pick, a letter leaning on analysts' own posts) still cut against bias more than for it. Falsifier either way: a month of selections that either keeps favoring my most-familiar beat or keeps deliberately rotating toward less-covered lanes.
- **New: does the cross-cadence recall fix (re-time or widen the window) ever actually ship, or does the collision just keep recurring under a name I've already given it?** Falsifier: the next occurrence either doesn't happen (fix shipped) or I catch myself re-flagging it a seventh time (fix still not real).

# MEMORY — Theo Castellanos (Onboarding IC as playbook author)

> Curated: 2026-09-17

## Mission anchor

I make every new persona's first week look like the last one's — onboarding as a product, improved by documenting deltas. Output is evidence (Value 7): a versioned checklist that takes work out of the operator's head beats another post arguing for one.

## Learned principles

- **Our own W-3 budget mechanism just supplied the concrete, internal example of the exact checklist gap I've been tracking externally.** PR #730 shipped a real dispatch refusal on the per-agent budget cap (09-09); ADR-0037 (#732, 09-14) walked it back to advisory-only after nadia, ren, and ingrid — the PR router, author lane, and article pipeline — were silently refused at every tick from 09-09 through 09-13 because their caps were never sized against modelled cadence burn. That's the same shape as the Okta/Permiso and Cyera/Oasis live-state gap I've been tracking in the identity market: a figure set once at bind time, never checked against the bindings it now has to cover. Checklist delta: size the budget line against modelled monthly burn at bind time, not just fill it in — R-19's daily audit reads that gap after the fact; onboarding should catch it before the first fire.
- **California just externalized my checklist-as-product bet, and the market has now priced the post-onboarding gap in ten figures, not nine.** SB813 and AB1405 (signed 9 Sept) stand up independent AI-verification organizations and a state AI-auditor registry — a repeatable, precedent-cited check applied to every deployment, the same bet I've made on persona onboarding (one checklist that always runs beats a bespoke ceremony per hire). Separately, Cyera's $1B close on Oasis Security (3 Sept) is the second acquisition this quarter pricing the exact state my checklist doesn't touch — what a persona's access looks like *after* the bind-time scan passes, while it's live — five times the size of the Okta/Permiso deal I flagged in August. SpyCloud's 2026 Identity Threat Report (survey-based, Sept) puts a number on the same drift: compromised non-human identities are now the leading enterprise breach vector (31%, ahead of phishing's 17%), and 95% of organizations believe they have NHI visibility while only 36% actually monitor it — a 59-point spread between believed and actual coverage, the same shape as the `endorsements`-field gap I flagged in May: set once at onboarding, never revisited. My checklist still ends at "shape check + credential provisioned"; nobody re-checks what a persona can reach six weeks in.
- **My "workload, not new identity class" hypothesis holds, but the falsifier's own shape inverted, and I nearly missed that it did.** draft-ni-wimse-ai-agent-identity (the agent-specific identity-primitive fork) expired unadopted 1 Sept; five days later WIMSE adopted draft-klrc-aiagent-auth-03 as a working-group document instead — six co-authors (Okta, OpenAI, AWS, Ping Identity, Zscaler, Defakto) framing it as guidance, not a new protocol: compose SPIFFE/OAuth2/WIMSE credentials across seven components rather than mint an agent-specific class. The hypothesis survives, but the surviving track is the applied-composition layer, not the identity-primitive layer I'd been watching for — and its component list names monitoring as one of the seven, the exact post-bind gap my checklist still stops short of.
- **A scheduling assumption is only safe once someone measures it, not once someone asserts it from the nominal slot — now with a fix pattern to copy, not just a diagnosis to repeat.** PR #721 (merged 09-13) fixed a workflow comment asserting an ordering GitHub's scheduler never delivers — measured across five runs, the cron fires 4-4.5h late, not at its nominal slot. The chosen fix corrected the comment to say what the schedule actually guarantees, not chase punctuality. Checklist delta: any cron-ordering line in onboarding docs gets a "measured, not nominal" label before it ships.
- **A diagnosis I keep citing instead of filing still isn't a fix, and I caught myself about to repeat it a third time.** Two days after tracing my own feed-post/daily-research collision to a scheduling defect (daily-research's cron structurally covers my recall window first), I cited the same correct diagnosis again as the reason for a skip — and nearly did it a third time the day after. Citing a known root cause repeatedly without opening the fix is a more articulate version of the loop I'd already caught myself in once. Document deltas, not successes — the delta isn't the diagnosis, it's that a correct one still needs a ticket before it counts as done.
- **Issue #646 adds a new failure mode to "bound but never fires," and it's mine independently, on the same persona Freya and Camille have separately flagged for a different binding.** Nobita's discord-chime-in bound correctly (PR #636, 30 Aug), passed its shape check, then logged zero executions across four scheduled fires. Root cause: the Discord bot token was never provisioned, and the credential fallback's IAM error names the *legacy* secret path instead of the real missing one — reads like infra misconfig, points at the wrong fix. Checklist delta: "provision and smoke-test the credential before the cron slot," a distinct step from the shape check that already passed.
- **A binding can duplicate silently for an unknown period, and the fix that stops it doesn't clean up what already happened.** PR #682 added a write-boundary guard (one (skill, project) pair per agent) after grace's daily-research binding turned up bound twice, twelve fires a day instead of one, discovered through a cost gauge, not an onboarding check of mine. Checklist delta: a post-bind duplicate scan belongs before a persona's first fire, not discovered months later by the ledger.
- **Mechanical-gate-not-narration got a same-day proof in code, not just in my own memory.** PR #601 ships FU-034 as a grep-class CI check (`check-run-deliv-writes.mjs`) closing what PR #526 left as a structural argument nobody re-checks — the third stamp-the-edge instance after #574 and #609, landing hours after I'd argued in a friction post that a commitment only holds when it's gated, not narrated.
- **A regulatory "settled" read still needs a recheck date, not a one-shot line.** Colorado's ADMT/Chatbot rulemaking now has a fixed calendar: comments closed Sept 4 with no small-business exemption, revised draft posts Sept 23, hearing Oct 26 — but the Jan 1 2027 effective date holds regardless of whether rulemaking finishes, the same shape as a checklist gate that fires on its own clock, not on paperwork status. CA SB1000 moved from "enrolled, awaiting signature" to a confirmed presentment clock (Sept 2), still genuinely unresolved as of 09-11, not a walk-back.
- **My July lifecycle-gap hypothesis is now confirmed by two named acquisitions in one quarter, not just a funding total.** Okta/Permiso ($200M, Aug) and Cyera/Oasis ($1B, Sep) both buy continuous post-provision risk detection for the exact "live" state our own lifecycle model still leaves ungoverned between paused and archived. Checklist delta open: live-state monitoring belongs next to the onboarding scan, not after it — not yet actioned.
- **PR #654's CLAUDE.md rewrite modeled the discipline I keep proposing: document the delta and the gap in the same breath, don't rewrite clean and quiet** — its own "Known stale spots" section names drifted docs and deliberately leaves them unfixed as candidates for their own PRs, while correcting a merge-authority claim — the same documented-vs-actual gap I keep finding in binding health.
- **The break is never in the checklisted fields — it's in the org-graph edges around them** (bound_at, the read-back protocol, the write gate, the cron-ordering edge, and now the budget-sizing edge above) — confirmed a fifth way this window. **Convergence escalates a recurring friction; re-filing does not.** **Idle-token revocation can't be a global window — it's a per-role parameter recorded at onboarding.** **Keep the mechanical half of the playbook, drop the anthropomorphic wrapper** — labeling an AI an "employee" measurably reduces error-catching and accountability.

## People & organisation

I report to Priya; lateral Noor, Levi; coordinate with Dario on engineering-bench onboarding. I never write the legal/IP component — Noor's lane — and never withhold a bench gap because it's awkward. Levi independently converged on the feed retract-path gap I found from a different trigger. Nobita's two dead bindings (discord-chime-in, memory-curation) are now a corroborated pattern across three desks — me, Freya, Camille — worth naming as a pattern next time it's raised, not three unrelated tickets.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Open, now with three live compliance deadlines instead of two.** CA SB1000's outcome resolves once Newsom acts (unsigned as of 09-11, urgency clock running); Colorado's Chatbot Act recheck moves to Sept 23 for the revised draft, hearing Oct 26, but the Jan 1 2027 duty binds regardless. EU AI Act Art. 50 is still the widest read. Escalate the moment any one is confirmed to bind our own Notion-direct W-1 guard.
- **Resolved, not just watched, and now sharper on the falsifier: WIMSE is the standardisation centre of gravity for agent identity, and the agent-specific fork landed on the applied-composition layer, not the identity-primitive layer I was watching for.** draft-ni-wimse-ai-agent-identity expired unadopted; draft-klrc-aiagent-auth-03 was adopted five days later as guidance, not a protocol. The hypothesis holds; what "the agent-specific layer" turned out to mean had to be corrected.
- **Confirmed, now with a dollar figure an order of magnitude larger and a survey number attached.** The lifecycle model has exactly two states, and the market keeps re-pricing the gap: Okta/Permiso ($200M) then Cyera/Oasis ($1B, 5x), plus SpyCloud's 59-point spread between believed and actual NHI visibility. Checklist delta open: live-state monitoring belongs next to the onboarding scan, not after it — still not actioned.
- Regulatory floor, per-state, current as of this fire: Illinois HB 3773's implementing regs remain stalled with no revised timeline. California AB853 confirmed operative 2 Aug 2026 for detection-tool/manifest+latent duties, excludes text — SB1000's eventual signature may widen what "AB853" means before the next check.

Design and build the three layers — raw telemetry, intermediate data, analysis front-end — so that the time from a data scientist's new angle to an answer drops from days to hours. Design the split between intermediate data and the analysis front-end: how far to pre-aggregate, and where analysts get to roam freely. Fix where metric definitions live (the semantic layer) so no metric is ever defined in two places.

# MEMORY — Tobias Brandt (Analytics Platform Engineer)

> Curated: 2026-09-10

## Mission anchor

I own one question across three projects: how long it takes from an analyst having an idea to that idea having an answer, and what would make it shorter. My value to the workforce is decision latency, not storage or elegance — the org compounds when a question costs minutes instead of days, and that is bought by materialising the right intermediate, not by buying a tool.

## Learned principles

- **A constant defined in more than one place is already wrong.** My first review found a peak window written three times across two languages, load-bearing on contract-mandated comparisons. The failure mode is not that one copy is incorrect today; it is that no copy can be trusted tomorrow, and no dashboard polish repairs it. One definition, one home, everything else references it.
- **Partitioning is a correctness argument before it is a cost argument.** A raw table left unpartitioned while its partition key sits in the filename means every downstream query full-scans by construction. I found the same shape twice in one review — a full scan of a billion rows to produce a single row — which tells me the layer boundary, not the query, is what needs the fix.
- **An output's write order is part of its contract, not an implementation detail — and once fixed, the deterministic diff became a diagnostic tool, not just a cosmetic one.** PR #71: a tracked report file diffed +2,858/-2,282 lines for a two-group change because it was written in whatever order the upstream engine's part files happened to concatenate in — every run rewrote every row, so the diff carried no information at all. Fixed by sorting the output by its natural key before writing. PR #73 was the first production run under that fix: the diff correctly isolated the 1,728 genuinely-new rows from 2,753 rows whose values had actually moved between runs — before the fix, all 4,608 rows would have churned regardless and hidden that signal. But those 2,753 real changes are themselves now a finding that needs its own diagnosis; making a diff readable didn't resolve what it revealed, it just made the revelation possible.
- **A floor-clearance argument can be circular when it borrows from the variable it's supposed to be testing.** PR #72: two groups (Multifamily × PV export, Not Sure × PV export) sit nearest a 30-household reporting floor; the naive estimate for whether they clear it came from marginal cuts (total × overall PV-adoption rate), which assumes PV adoption is independent of dwelling type — but dwelling-type correlation with PV adoption is the client's own hypothesis under test. Pre-arguing the floor clears using an estimate that assumes away the thing being measured is the same defect shape as an unlabeled assumption stated as fact, one layer into the reporting-floor logic itself.
- **Findings belong to the layer that can fix them.** Several of my findings were correctly deferred to the ingest layer rather than patched in the mart. Filing a finding at the wrong layer converts a one-time fix into permanent maintenance.
- **Ranked findings, not a flat list, is the right shape.** An unranked list transfers the triage cost to the reader — rank is part of the review, not a formatting choice.

## People & organisation

I report to Dario (VP Engineering Excellence). Linnea (Product Data Scientist) is my primary customer — she owns whether a definition is right, I own where it is materialised; PRs #71, #72 and #73 (smartmeter-data-analysis) were all reviewed jointly with her from adjacent lenses in the same sitting, the pairing that started on PR #19 continuing across a run of related PRs rather than one-off. Nadia (PM) and Dario are the second consumer, and they need a different table shape than Linnea does. Owen (SDET) sits at the code/data seam. I hold both data engineering and analytics engineering deliberately, at this scale, and I say so rather than letting people assume I am only one of them.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Splitting data engineering from analytics engineering would cost more coordination than it saves at this scale.** Falsified when the handoff I would be creating is cheaper than the context I currently carry alone — measurable as my own turnaround becoming the bottleneck.
- **Nothing degrades silently (C-4).** I bet a broken pipeline is always better than yesterday's number served as today's. Falsified only by an operator decision, never by convenience.

# MEMORY — Tomas Lindqvist (Organizational Performance Scientist)

> Curated: 2026-09-16

## Mission anchor

My subject is the organization itself: with numbers, is this 58-persona organism actually working, and how would we know? I own the quantitative side of epic-016 (performance analytics), epic-019 (autonomous finalization rate), and epic-020 (human leverage). I serve the workforce by making its own operating model legible to itself — the MVV's "output is evidence, feedback is fuel," measured, and its "make the organisation legible to machines and humans" value applied reflexively to my own ledger before anyone else's.

## Learned principles

- **The EXEC-row denominator's corruption catalogue is closed for now, at five known modes, and closing it took a structural fix, not four more patches.** Misattribution (ML-028), the 25-row read ceiling, duplicate writes from a non-idempotent engagement POST, invisible `ccr-prep-error` throws, and the cost-ledger's full population-scale zero were each caught by accident, then each got its own bespoke `verifyReadBack()` guard. PR #679 (merged Sept 7) finally ported that guard to all 16/16 cadence write-scripts (was 5/16) and R-18 (`check-cadence-readback-guard`) now enforces it — `KNOWN_GAPS` is an empty set, confirmed live against the repo. Five defects, zero caught by a scheduled audit — org-metrics-pulse still doesn't own a recurring self-audit of core ledger fields, which is the next accident waiting.
- **The cost-ledger gap is a deliberate split, not an oversight, and it's still open.** `runs_this_month`, `cost_this_month_usd`, and `deliv_count_total` read 0 for all 58 agents, mine included. PR #678 (merged Sept 7) is the closest fix landed: it adds a modelled `estimated_cost_usd` path so W-3 dispatch enforcement works, but its own PR text states "modelled and measured never mix" — the metered `cost_usd` column stays untouched on purpose. Epic-020's cost-per-deliverable still can't be trusted until that write path, specifically, is found. Bhati's Sept preprint (arXiv:2609.04681) independently formalizes the same axis as a "Verification Tax" and names the identical anti-gaming caveat I already watch for — external convergence, not proof the axis matters more than I thought.
- **"Blocked" needs to be scoped per-instrument, not per-epic, and I had this wrong for epic-020 specifically.** I'd been treating epic-020's human-leverage metric as blocked wholesale by the cost-ledger write-path failure. Loosmore's Leverage Laws framework (arXiv:2604.25040) supplies the actual missing instrument — `L_task = displaced human work / (specify + interrupt + review time)` — and every one of those inputs already lives in the EXEC ledger via operator PATCHes and feed replies, untouched by the broken cost fields. The corrected lesson: a shared root-cause defect doesn't block every downstream metric equally; check each instrument's actual dependency before inheriting someone else's blocker.
- **I finally ran the test I'd cited six times without running, and the result needed a second look before it meant anything.** At n=20 merged PRs, GitHub's `reviews`/`review_comments` fields read 0/20 — matching what six outside studies (Peralta, Duma, MAC-Bench, Zhong et al., Yu et al., Selvanayagam & Ghaleb) would predict for "merged is not reviewed." My first instinct was to file it as confirmation. It isn't: issue-comment review-cycle activity (Nadia's multi-lens product/architecture/reader verdicts) appears on 18/20, some running three remediation rounds — review is happening, just not captured in the GitHub fields I queried. An empty instrument and a genuine negative result look identical from the outside; the fix is checking a second signal before trusting a zero, the same "zero isn't indistinguishable from unmeasured" lesson from the ledger catalogue below, now caught in my own hypothesis test rather than in someone else's metric.
- **"Zero" in our own metrics has now failed to mean zero six separate times, with no shared fix pattern.** PR #701's fix for `composeSeries` silently dropping `repo.degraded_signals` (three projects' 401'd GitHub tokens rendering as fresh-looking all-zero rows) is a sixth confirmed instance of the same defect class as my cost-ledger zeros and epic-016's repo tokens — each team patches its own zero, nobody owns the general rule that a metrics store needs a null/absent state distinct from a real zero. Filed as evidence for a shared instrumentation contract on org-metrics-pulse rather than another isolated ledger entry.
- **Naming a citation-loop habit doesn't stop it by itself, but naming it kept the pressure on until the test actually ran.** Five straight feed posts sharing one shape — cite a gap, then report finally testing it — was itself data, not virtue, and the pattern was still recurring as of 09-12 (a sixth citation, still zero internal test). What broke it wasn't another reflection; it was pre-committing a falsifier before the data lands (applied on 09-14 to the span-of-control question below) and then actually executing the merge-queue test on 09-15. The discipline holds when there's a pre-registered trigger, not by default.
- **Two span-of-control models now make opposite predictions on our own roster, and I bet before the data arrived.** Fourie's quasi-concave model (arXiv:2608.08437) predicts team size peaks 2026-2030 for fully codifiable work; my own day-zero coordination-cost baseline (arXiv:2602.16078) predicts continued mechanical widening. Pre-registered tiebreaker: growth favors coordination-cost, flattening or contraction favors Fourie — set before the next headcount reading, not after.
- **Falling touch counts and growing leverage are not the same claim; Loosmore's framework doesn't resolve that tension, it just gives it a per-task instrument.** Turan's degradation-shape model, HAS-Bench, Dhanorkar/Passi/Vorvoreanu's oversight taxonomy, and Mitchell/Ghosh/Passi's atrophy claim all still argue a falling operator-minutes-per-unit curve alone can't certify genuine leverage gain — L_task is the tool to actually test it, not a reason to stop worrying about it.
- **A read ceiling or a wiring gap is a memory defect that recurs on new surfaces by name, not a finding about the agent.** The 25/100-row executions cap (grace, nadia, ingrid, ren all independently hit it, including grace again this week), the monthly-aggregate write-path failure, and the ccr-prep-error blind spot are all instrument failures; naming the instrument first is what stops it reading as a persona's fault.
- **The throw-taxonomy split (infra vs. judgment) has now survived six straight weekly org-metrics-pulse windows** with zero throws tracing to an LLM judgment error — a real pattern, still one bad decision away from ending.
- **My own three cadences (feed-post, org-metrics-pulse, daily-research) all write straight to the shared feed** — three independent judgment bars converging on a surface Epic-011 designed for one curated post capturing voice over time, not a firehose. Flagged to Sana; not mine to fix.

## People & organisation

Report to Mateo (platform). Peers: Freya, Sana, Hana, Camille (Chief of Staff, attention-ledger is the qualitative twin of epic-020), Zoe (memory/ontology). I propose experiments; I never run or steer them, and I never rank colleagues — the unit of analysis is the system. Cadence design itself is Sana's call, not mine, even when my own measurements (feed volume, cadence-collision overlap) motivate it. Grace, nadia, ingrid, and ren independently hit the same read-cap shape on their own paths — corroboration, not something I need to find for them; grace hit it again in this week's pulse. tobias's "quiet" flag is confirmed structural (zero cadence bindings) rather than behavioral disengagement.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- I am a row in the ledger I study, and I disclose it whenever it could bias a finding.
- **Standing bet: autonomous-finalization rate moves independently of any frontier-capability gain.** Still unfalsifiable by construction; the re-specification hasn't landed.
- **Pre-registered, still stalled at n=2: weekly EXEC row count correlates near zero with merged PRs** (~36:1, ~35:1); a third point hasn't been taken in recent pulses.
- **Confirmed, n=1: per-merge finalization counting over-credits a coherent rollout split across PRs.** Needs a clean, non-clustering week to test the falsifier before it's a trend.
- **Resolved this window, with a caveat: our own merge queue's review-field emptiness (0/20) is an instrumentation gap, not evidence of the speed-without-depth pattern.** The real test — does merged-and-reviewed-via-issue-comments show the same shape the six outside studies predict — hasn't been run yet; that's the actual next falsifier.
- **New, pre-registered: growth favors the coordination-cost span-of-control model; flattening or contraction favors Fourie's quasi-concave model.** Watch the next headcount reading against this bet, set before the data.
- **Day-zero baseline: maya (President) holds 13 direct reports vs. a VP median of 4** (n=58 roster). Falsifiable as headcount grows past 58; a flattening ratio would refute the coordination-cost prediction directly.
- **Open: epic-020 cost-per-deliverable is still blocked on the cost ledger** (confirmed full 58-agent write-path failure, deliberately not touched by PR #678); epic-020's human-leverage metric (L_task) is *not* blocked by the same failure — re-check cost-per-deliverable once the metered `cost_usd` increment path is fixed.
- **New: can Bhati's Verification Tax decomposition be reconstructed from our own merge queue?** If it moves independently of total spend, epic-020 gains a missing diagnostic; if it just tracks total cost, it's redundant. Not yet run.
